claims.text: The proposed rare-earth-free alloy system is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi produced by selective laser melting.
Selective laser melting is used as a rapid-solidification processing route.
The as-fabricated alloy contains a high density of uniformly distributed nanoscale precipitates.
Mn2O3 is a possible nanoscale precipitate in the proposed alloy.
Fine nanoscale precipitates create localized strain fields that couple to adjacent magnetic domains.
Precipitate-induced magnetoelastic coupling lowers the energy barrier for a sharp low-field magnetostructural transition.
Precipitate-induced strain modifies the energy landscape for magnetization reversal.
The facilitated magnetostructural transition increases the magnetic entropy change and magnetocaloric response at applied fields below about 0.5 T.
The fine precipitate dispersion promotes rapid heat exchange or effective thermal transport.
The precipitate-mediated strain fields reduce magnetic or magnetostructural hysteresis.
The fine precipitate dispersion helps sustain mechanical stability.
Controlled annealing can coarsen or reduce the density of the nanoscale precipitates without changing the overall alloy composition.
Relative to the annealed material, the as-fabricated fine-precipitate material will have a larger low-field magnetocaloric response.
Relative to the annealed material, the as-fabricated fine-precipitate material will show a sharper transition.
Relative to the annealed material, the as-fabricated fine-precipitate material will show lower hysteresis.
Coarsening or reducing the precipitate density will reduce the magnetocaloric response and increase hysteresis.

The proposed relationships should apply near the magnetic transition in equiatomic or compositionally similar rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys containing nanoscale precipitates and exposed to low applied fields.
